source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 17 January 1923, p. 6 ("Municipal elections (continued from page 5)"); Belfast News-Letter, 6 January 1923, p. 5 ("Ulster local elections: nominations in Belfast")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: figures read from the page images of the News-Letter's ward results (INA block images) and checked against the Irish News; names and full forms from the News-Letter's list of nominations; unopposed members are the only remaining nominees for the seats after the withdrawals reported on 8 January

note: Election of the whole of Belfast Corporation (an alderman and three councillors in each of the 15 wards) by direct vote, proportional representation having been abolished; nominations 5 January, poll Monday 15 January 1923, counted 16 January. Eight aldermen and nine councillors (St Anne's, Pottinger and Windsor) were returned unopposed at nomination, and withdrawals left the Duncairn and Victoria councillors unopposed (Belfast News-Letter, 6 and 8 January 1923). State of parties in the new Corporation: Official Unionists 43, Independent Unionists 7, Nationalists 3, Labour 2 (News-Letter, 17 January 1923).
